execution_note: The five SPAdes --isolate drafts are those of the regeneration with release 1.0.1 (assembled by the closed-genome stage of its tier calibration with 4 threads and a 14 GB memory cap, and reused by its 23S analysis); they were copied with unchanged checksums, and the workflow keeps an existing draft, so memory_gb below applied to no assembly in this run. The GenBank records of the closed genomes are the files that regeneration downloaded. The reads were mapped again and every later stage was run again. The GFA checksums are recorded in workflow_provenance.json.
interpretation: The aggregate-depth rule classified 5 of 5 two-copy 23S loci as MULTICOPY_DEPTH and 0 of 5 single-copy gyrB controls as MULTICOPY_DEPTH. Observed 23S depth ratios were 2.546-3.221. The copy-number consensus was an exact, supported count of two for 0 of 5 23S loci, a lower bound (copy_number_kind LOWER_BOUND) for 1, and an exact, supported count of one for 5 of 5 gyrB controls. 23S loci with copy_number_status REVIEW: Hpfe0001, Hpfe0002, Hpfe0003, Hpfe0006. In 4 of them (Hpfe0001, Hpfe0002, Hpfe0003, Hpfe0006) the graph holds two flanking contexts and the depth-ratio interval excludes two; release 1.0.2 returns such a count for review, with copy_number_lower_bound equal to the count and no upper bound, where release 1.0.1 returned SUPPORTED with both bounds equal to the count. all_primary_criteria_passed is false. The panel informed the design of the graph method; it is a biological demonstration, not an independent performance estimate.
